title: Theories of schooling: super-domains and sub-domains

source.label: Eirdosh & Hanisch (2023), a community science model for interdisciplinary evolution education and school improvement

note: The domain names and one-line meanings follow the Theories of Schooling widget (widgets/schooling/schooling.js). Other models can use the same file shape, so the atlas can show a different set of domains.
superHint: Broad ideas about people and societies that inform how people think about schooling
subHint: The aspects of schooling people reason about

supers.name: Human origins, diversity and flexibility
supers.means: Broad claims about where human behaviour and thinking come from, how much people differ, and how flexible human nature is. In the Guide this is the evolutionary background: Tinbergen's four questions and comparisons with other species and with our ancestors. The umbrella the other four sit under.
supers.ask: Which beliefs about human nature sit behind the way our school is run?

supers.name: Human development
supers.means: How people grow, learn and change over a lifetime: how children's understanding builds up and changes, how thinking about thinking develops, and how competence is built.
supers.ask: What do the adults and students here believe about how young people learn best?

supers.name: Cultural evolution
supers.means: How cultures, institutions and practices change, spread and persist: social learning, cumulative culture, norms and innovation. For schools this includes the account of curriculum change as an evolutionary process.
supers.ask: Which school traditions have lasted, and who benefits from them?

supers.name: Self
supers.means: What a person is and can become: agency, identity, motivation, emotion, beliefs about oneself and the ability to watch one's own thinking.
supers.ask: What does it mean to be a good student here, and who decided that?

supers.name: Society
supers.means: How groups and societies work and what people owe each other: cooperation, conflict, fairness, shared resources, institutions and sustainability.
supers.ask: What do people in our community expect school to do for society?

subs.name: Theories of school origins
subs.means: Where schools, schooling and curricula came from and why they exist, including how teaching and social learning arose before schools.
subs.ask: Why was our school founded, and who is it meant to serve?

subs.name: Theories of school futures
subs.means: How schooling could or should change: trends such as artificial intelligence and climate change, futures thinking taught in school, and the idea that education is studied as it could be.
subs.ask: What would our school look like if students designed it?

subs.name: Theories of adaptive fit
subs.means: How well schools, curricula and teaching fit the people, places and needs they serve, including the mismatches: overload, separated subjects, well-being, culture and surroundings.
subs.ask: Where does school fit our lives well, and where does it clash with them?

subs.name: Theories of optimal schooling
subs.means: What good teaching, learning and curriculum look like: aims and competencies, what to teach, how to teach it, how learning progresses and how to assess it.
subs.ask: What would the best school day look like, and for whom?

subs.name: Theories of school improvement
subs.means: How schools and school systems get better and who does it: design labs and community science labs, teacher development, the part students and teachers play, and curriculum modelling.
subs.ask: How do people here think change happens, and who gets to start it?

elementTypes.name: Statement about how things are
elementTypes.means: A claim, finding or theory about people, learning, culture or schooling.

elementTypes.name: Observation about schools or curricula
elementTypes.means: What a school, curriculum or textbook contains or does today.

elementTypes.name: Proposal for teaching or schooling
elementTypes.means: A proposal for how to teach, what to teach or how to organise schooling.

elementTypes.name: Aim
elementTypes.means: A goal that schooling or teaching should serve.

elementTypes.name: Teaching practice
elementTypes.means: A way of teaching or a teaching material: a method, a lesson or a resource used in classrooms.

elementTypes.name: Open question
elementTypes.means: A question that research or design work still has to answer.

elementTypes.name: Key idea
elementTypes.means: A concept that the theory uses and defines.

flow.superSub: broad ideas about people and societies

links.note: First draft of how the domains relate. These are proposals for the authors to confirm, change or remove. A theory file can add its own links.

super.means: What is true of human nature in general both limits and enables how people develop.
What is true of human nature in general shapes how cultures can change.
What is true of human nature in general shapes what a person is and can become.
What is true of human nature in general shapes how societies can work.
People form a sense of self as they grow, and that sense of self guides how they go on to learn.
Learning passes culture on to each new generation, and culture shapes what children learn.
Changing practices and institutions are what societies are made of.
What a society expects of children and schools frames how young people are raised.
Ideas of the self differ between societies, and a society depends on what its members expect of themselves and each other.

sub.means: How schools came to be explains much of how well they fit people’s lives today.
Seeing where schooling fits poorly shows what better schooling would have to do.
Ideas of the best possible schooling set the direction for improvement work.
Improvement work changes schools, and so changes which futures can happen.
Pictures of possible futures change what people think the best schooling would be.
Improvements change how well schools fit the people they serve.
